title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text: What drives first-year MLB arbitration salaries for starting pitchers?

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text: What drives first-year MLB arbitration salaries for starting pitchers?

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Project Overview
This project uses arbitration salary data and pitching performance metrics to estimate which factors most influence first-year arbitration salaries.
The goal is to connect econometric modeling with a real baseball operations question: how players are valued during the arbitration process.

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Data

Salary data: Spotrac
Performance data: Fangraphs / Statcast
Sample: First-year arbitration and Super Two starting pitchers
Years: 2016–2026
Observations: 124 pitchers

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Model
I estimated an OLS regression using log salary as the dependent variable.
Independent variables included:

Innings Pitched (IP)
Strikeout Rate (K%)
Walk Rate (BB%)
ERA
Year fixed effects

The logarithmic specification allows coefficients to be interpreted approximately as percentage changes in salary and helps address right-skewness in arbitration salary distributions.
The model estimated how pitcher performance metrics were associated with arbitration outcomes while controlling for season-level differences.

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Key Findings

Workload was strongly rewarded in arbitration.
10 additional innings pitched were associated with roughly a 5.8% increase in salary.
ERA remained highly influential.
One additional run of ERA was associated with roughly an 11% decrease in salary.
Strikeout rate showed moderate evidence of positive salary impact.
The model underpredicted elite performers such as Shane Bieber, Corbin Burnes, and Hunter Brown.

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Baseball Interpretation
The results suggest that first-year arbitration salaries still reward traditional indicators such as innings pitched and ERA.
This matters because arbitration is not just a pure projection system. It reflects performance, precedent, role, reputation, and comparable-player arguments.

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Limitations
Important omitted variables may include:

WAR
Awards
Injuries
Role changes
Reputation
Comparable-player effects
Team/player negotiation context

title: MLB Arbitration OLS Model
text:
Next Steps
Future versions of this project could:

Add WAR and advanced metrics
Compare traditional vs modern statistics
Use LASSO to evaluate variable selection
Analyze residuals to identify overpaid and underpaid arbitration cases
Build comparable-player groups
